role: Research fellow in criminal law; deputy director (1992–1995)
organization: Legal Institute of the Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic (Právnický inštitút Ministerstva spravodlivosti SR)
description: According to the TASR profile, he worked at the ministry's Legal Institute as a researcher in criminal law and was its deputy director from 1992 to 1995. E15 states that he worked at the institute until 1995.

role: Government agent representing Slovakia before the European Court of Human Rights and the European Commission of Human Rights
organization: Government of the Slovak Republic (Ministry of Justice)
description: Served as the agent representing the Slovak Republic in proceedings before the European Court of Human Rights and the European Commission of Human Rights in Strasbourg from 1994 to 2000, according to TASR.

organization: Communist Party of Slovakia / Communist Party of Czechoslovakia (KSS/KSČ)
description: TASR dates his membership of the Communist Party of Slovakia to 1987–1990; E15 and Wikipedia state that he joined the Communist Party in 1986.

organization: Party of the Democratic Left (Strana demokratickej ľavice, SDĽ)
description: Joined the SDĽ, the post-communist successor party, on its creation in 1990 and was elected to parliament on its lists in 1992, 1994 (Spoločná voľba coalition) and 1998. TASR gives his vice-chairmanship as 1996–1999 (Wikipedia says he was elected deputy chairman in 1998). He left the party in 1999.

role: Member of the Slovak National Council / National Council of the Slovak Republic
organization: Slovenská národná rada / Národná rada Slovenskej republiky
description: Elected in 1992 (Slovak National Council, SDĽ list), re-elected in 1994 (Spoločná voľba list) and 1998 (SDĽ) to the National Council, and in 2002 as leader of Smer, which sat in opposition to the Dzurinda government. His mandate ended when he became Prime Minister in July 2006.

role: Member of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (substitute 1993–1999; representative 1999–2000 and 2003–2005)
organization: Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE), Slovak delegation
description: PACE records list him as a substitute member for the Slovak Republic from 27 September 1993 to 25 January 1999, and as a representative from 25 January 1999 to 24 January 2000 and from 27 January 2003 to 20 June 2005.

Presented the new party Smer on 29 October 1999 and has chaired it since (TASR). Smer later absorbed several small left-wing parties, including the SDĽ, and took the name SMER – sociálna demokracia (E15, Wikipedia). As of October 2026 he remains party chairman.

Headed a coalition of Smer-SD, the Slovak National Party (SNS) and ĽS-HZDS formed after the June 2006 election. Slovakia joined the Schengen area (December 2007) and adopted the euro (1 January 2009) during this term.

role: Deputy Speaker of the National Council and leader of the largest opposition party
description: Smer-SD won the June 2010 election with 34.79% but Fico could not form a majority; a centre-right coalition led by Iveta Radičová took office and he became a deputy speaker of parliament as leader of the main opposition party.
Formed the first single-party government since 1993 after Smer-SD won 83 of 150 seats in the March 2012 early election.

Headed a coalition of Smer-SD, SNS, Most-Híd and (initially) #Sieť; Slovakia held the Presidency of the Council of the EU in the second half of 2016. He resigned after the murder of Ján Kuciak and Martina Kušnírová; President Andrej Kiska accepted the resignation on 15 March 2018 and appointed Peter Pellegrini's government on 22 March 2018.

role: Member of the National Council (opposition from 2020)
description: Returned to parliament after leaving the premiership while remaining Smer-SD chairman; re-elected in February 2020, when Smer-SD went into opposition. In May 2022 parliament did not consent to his custody in the criminal case later annulled by the Prosecutor General (see justice).
Appointed by President Zuzana Čaputová on 25 October 2023 at the head of a coalition of Smer-SD, Hlas-SD and the SNS, after Smer-SD won the 30 September 2023 election. In office as of October 2026.

role: Prime Minister entrusted with running the Ministry of the Environment
organization: Ministry of the Environment of the Slovak Republic (Ministerstvo životného prostredia SR)
description: After parliament passed a motion of no confidence in Environment Minister Tomáš Taraba, supported by the coalition SNS together with the opposition, President Peter Pellegrini dismissed Taraba on 30 September 2026 and entrusted Prime Minister Robert Fico with running the ministry (poverenie predsedu vlády SR riadením Ministerstva životného prostredia SR). On 21 October 2026 the President declined to appoint the SNS nominee Filip Kuffa and asked the Prime Minister for a new nomination, so Fico remained in charge of the ministry as of that date.
